claim: In a retrospective 8-centre real-world RNS cohort (n=150), median seizure reduction was 67% at 1 year, 75% at 2 years, 82% at >=3 years and 74% at last follow-up (mean 2.3 y); 18% reported clinical seizure freedom.

supporting_passages: One hundred fifty patients met the criteria for analysis.

The median reduction in seizures was 67% (interquartile range [IQR] = 33%-93%, n = 149) at 1 year, 75% (IQR = 50%-94%, n = 93) at 2 years, 82% (IQR = 50%-96%, n = 38) at ≥3 years, and 74% (IQR = 50%-96%, n = 150) at last follow-up (mean = 2.3 years).
Thirty-five percent of patients had a ≥90% seizure frequency reduction, and 18% of patients reported being clinically seizure-free at last follow-up.

contradictions: Outcomes exceed pivotal/LTT trial at matched timepoints (e.g. 67% vs 44% at 1 y) - authors attribute to improved programming; retrospective design and shrinking n (38 at >=3 y) limit comparability.
Possible patient overlap with later multicenter retrospective series (e.g. Sadeghzadeh 2026) and with RNS trial patients at the same centers is not reported - to_verify.
